stops.note: Cicero's dialogue De Natura Deorum (45 BC) debates what the gods (dei) are and whether they care about humans
older spelling of deus; Portuguese traders settled Macau from 1557, the first European foothold on the China coast
the trade pidgin of Canton, where the Qing confined Western trade under the Canton System from 1757, reshaped deos into joss, applied to Chinese deities and their images
China traders brought home 'joss stick' and 'joss house'; the Bendigo Joss House in Australia, built by gold-rush Chinese miners in the 1860s, still stands

current_meaning: a Chinese religious image; luck (as in 'joss stick', 'joss house')
